newsitem.title: UK: Red Cross to raise North Korea food aid fivefold.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross to raise North Korea food aid fivefold.

text.p: The Red Cross, alarmed at widespread hunger in North Korea with some people reduced to eating cooked grassroots and tree bark, said on Saturday it planned to increase fivefold its food aid programme for the country.
From July 1 for at least five months, food will be supplied to around 700,000 people in the Asian Communist state, up from 139,000 at present, the British Red Cross said in a statement.
It said the International Federation of the humanitarian agency had taken the decision after a visit to the country by three officials led by British International Director Geoff Dennis.
The statement said the three officials had found the food shortage "very visible", with warehouses practically empty and malnourished children and elderly people in many places.
"People cooking grassroots and bark for survival or as a supplement to the little food they had was a common sight," it said.
"The most critical period is from now until the next harvest and therefore we have put all our efforts into expanding our relief operation in the coming months," Dennis said.
He said the money to increase the food programme had come from a number of sources, including substantial donations from the South Korean Red Cross.
The statement said North Korea's health system had "completely collapsed", so the Red Cross also planned to implement a one-year programme to supply essential drugs.

The Red Cross has been supplying food to vulnerable people, such as pregnant women, the elderly and the disabled, in 15 North Korean counties since the country suffered its worst on record floods in 1995.
Further floods last year left half a million people homeless and affected some 30 percent of the country's arable land.
The statement said there will now be more beneficiaries in each county, and four new areas will be added to the operation -- Anju, Sunchon, Kujang and the industrial town of Wonsan.
